html:
The Mombasa to Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway is a line of about 470 km, opened in 2017, that links the port of Mombasa on the Indian Ocean with Nairobi, the capital of Kenya. It was the country's largest infrastructure project since independence.

It runs roughly parallel to the colonial metre gauge Uganda Railway, built by the British from 1896 and nicknamed the Lunatic Express. That old line had decayed, and most freight from the port moved by truck on a crowded highway.

The new line was built by the China Road and Bridge Corporation and paid for mostly with loans from the Export-Import Bank of China, at a cost of over three billion US dollars. It is an early large project of the Belt and Road Initiative in Africa. Its passenger service, the Madaraka Express, cut the trip to about five hours.

An extension reached Naivasha in 2019, but money ran out before the line got to Uganda. Critics point to the high cost, the debt, and rules that forced importers to use the train.
